profile.what: State-promoted (Government of Gujarat, through Gujarat State Investments Ltd, 37.84%) maker of fertilisers and industrial chemicals, incorporated 1962 as India's first joint-sector fertiliser company. Two complexes: Fertilizernagar, Vadodara (ammonia, urea, ammonium sulphate, APS, sulphuric acid, caprolactam, nylon-6, melamine, methanol, MEK oxime, HX crystal) and Sikka, Jamnagar (DAP/APS trains, own jetty and ammonia storage used for imports). Plus GSFC Agrotech (distribution subsidiary), a 99-year lease on 276.7 ha at Dahej (Nov-2025) and a large portfolio of shares in other Gujarat PSUs.
profile.segments: Fertilizer products (78% of FY26 revenue): urea (3.25 lakh t sold), ammonium sulphate (5.76 lakh t, record), APS 20:20:0:13 (7.16 lakh t, record), DAP (1.46 lakh t), NPK, plus traded urea (3.20 lakh t) and P&K (1.43 lakh t). Industrial products (22%): caprolactam (54,671 t sold externally; the rest goes into nylon-6), nylon-6 (35,010 t), melamine (38,780 t), methanol, MEK oxime, HX crystal, technical-grade urea and traded ammonia.

q1fy27.borrowingsJun26: About ₹500 cr at 30-Jun-2026; "no cash surplus" (cash went into raw materials, finished goods and DAP subsidy that arrives ~6 months after sale)

q1fy27.volumesMix: Manufactured 3.53 lakh t (APS 1.01, AS 0.96, urea 0.96, DAP 0.60), traded P&K 1.31, traded urea 0.42

points: Ammonia from own gas-based plants (Ammonia-III and IV at 100%); gas price rises are passed through in the urea subsidy.
Sulphur ~$850/t; sulphuric acid stock carried from long-term contracts (Reliance, Nayara, BPCL, IOCL), but supply not 100% and at high rates; AS imported to fill gaps.

DAP and urea margins "fully protected" by the government (special package for DAP); NPK/APS margins may move "plus minus 5% to 10%"; IP segment expected to compensate (capro-benzene spread above $800/t in May vs ~$670/t in Q4).
C-Train conversion (1,300-1,400 TPD DAP train to swing DAP/APS) expected in July-August 2026.
Sulphur ~₹82,000/t average in Q1, above ₹115,000/t by mid-August; international sulphur above $1,000/t; P2O5 $1,700/t.
DAP special package: import cost plus a 4% margin; urea fully covered; APS/NPK/AS "a real uncomfort"; some AS imported because it is not viable to make.
FY27 fertiliser sales budget "more than 22 lakh metric ton" incl. trading.
Rabi NBS rates due from 1-Oct; management hopes for an increase.
Capro-benzene spread above $800/t; melamine output stopped (Chinese imports); anti-dumping duty sought.
BCG cost programme saved ₹20-25 cr in Q1; Dahej integrated complex (fertiliser and industrial products) to be disclosed after technology tie-up and financial model; no buyback planned.

history.event: Incorporated as India's first joint-sector fertiliser company; ammonia-urea at Vadodara (1967)
history.impact: The base of the Vadodara complex

history.event: Caprolactam, nylon-6, melamine and sulphuric acid added; Sikka (Jamnagar) DAP unit and jetty (jetty operating since 1987)
history.impact: Two segments; Sikka gives an import gateway for ammonia, acid and DAP

history.event: New melamine capacity ramps up (melamine sales 14,000 t in FY19 to 48,000 t in FY22); borrowings cut from ₹1,559 cr (Mar-20) to ₹6 cr (Mar-22)
history.impact: Debt-free; IP EBIT ₹524 cr in FY22
Fertiliser EBIT ₹1,460 cr and EPS ₹31.8 in FY23 (record)

history.event: Prices and subsidies fall; Chinese caprolactam and melamine exports depress spreads; GSFC tenders 15.93 lakh GNFC shares in GNFC's buyback (₹123 cr)
HX crystal plant (20 TPD) starts (Oct-2024); GIPCL holding raised to 2.43 cr shares
Urea-II revamp, SA-V acid plant and 15 MW solar commissioned (₹674 cr); Dahej land lease; three managing directors in the year
history.impact: Gross block +27%; EPS ₹16.9; IP EBIT ₹200 cr (best in four years)

history.event: Middle East supply shock: sulphur, ammonia and P2O5 spike; DAP special package; capro-benzene spread $816/t
history.impact: Revenue +64%, PAT +14%; fertiliser EBIT margin 4.1%; ₹500 cr borrowed

history.event: GSPC-Gujarat Gas merger (effective 1-May-2026) and GSPL Transmission demerger (record date 2-Jul-2026)
history.impact: GSFC's 2.35 cr GSPC shares become 7.7 lakh Gujarat Energy shares; it also receives ~1.59 cr GSPL Transmission shares

governance.kmpPay: KMP remuneration ₹1.91 cr in FY26 (₹2.20 cr FY25)
governance.auditor: CNK & Associates LLP (statutory); subsidy receivable recoverability is a key audit matter
governance.policy: Gujarat Finance Department resolution (Apr-2023): state PSUs to pay the higher of 30% of profit or 5% of net worth as dividend and consider buybacks when net worth > ₹2,000 cr and cash > ₹1,000 cr, unless exempted; GSFC pays ~30% of profit (~1.6% of net worth)

accounting: Investments in listed and unlisted shares are at fair value through OCI: price moves go to reserves, not profit; only dividends hit the P&L.
Indian Potash (unlisted) revalued from ₹723 cr to ₹1,275 cr in FY26 (level-3 valuation).
Subsidy income ₹4,514 cr (41% of revenue) recognised on notified rates; receivable ₹1,453 cr at Mar-26 is a key audit matter.
Contingent liabilities "Other" rose to ₹1,333 cr (₹765 cr) without a breakdown in the notes.
₹1,160 cr of deposits with financial institutions sit in other current financial assets, not cash.
